value.hook: Open before rendering or admitting a seat id, instance, project or request id, before printing a repair command built from stored rows, or before testing hostile legacy rows (F127, F132, F135)
value.title: Rendering stored values: one grammar, commands are a sink too, seeding legacy rows

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Adds to the "Daemon-authored text and bounded reads" note, from #182, #185 (three rounds) and F135.

1. One grammar per kind, shared by render and admission. Directory names (project, role, holding instance) use pij_core::render::is_name ([a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}); seat ids use SeatId::is_canonical (F127); msg ids use render::msg_id. F135's assign check calls the same is_name, so anything recorded always shows as itself. A second, parallel grammar (#184's memory-turn `word`) became a merge conflict and a review finding. Before choosing a grammar, check every live value read-only (sqlite3 "file:$HOME/.pij-rs/pij.sqlite?mode=ro", plus the governance holders and outputs documents).
2. A rendered listing isn't enough: printed commands and `next` are sinks too. shell_word quoting keeps a newline intact inside the quotes. When a stored seat or instance can't be shown, choose a canonical alternative (the first canonical holder), print no command, or use a placeholder (<seat>). Never print a command built from the raw value. Bobcat blocked #185 twice on exactly this: several-holders fallbacks and picture actions_weighing (revive/assign).
3. Values travel. A broad role send copies the holding's stored instance into request.instance, and a restart requeue keeps it. So every text that names a request's address must render it: RoleAddress::display does it once.
4. Leave structured JSON data that operators act on (the view's lineage/live) as stored, JSON-escaped. Render prose and commands. Say so in the PR body.
5. Seeding legacy rows in tests:
   - Store-read paths: rig.store.record_assignment_committed with community::holders::seat_role_for(role), or role sends refuse E-RS-ROLE-MISMATCH. Register a non-canonical seat straight in the registry.
   - Paths that read the governance holders document (retire): assign a valid key, rewrite it in repo.gov's holders.dd.json, then commit.
   - Release and rebuild stay loose so a legacy row can still be ended.
6. Test traps:
   - response.to_string().contains("pij send") matches the envelope's own "command" field, so assert on meta and details.next.
   - cargo test takes several filters only after `--` (`test -p pij-daemon --lib -- a b`); before it, cargo errors and a grep pipeline prints nothing.
   - A mutant only bites when the fixture makes the guarded row the one a command would pick. Order hostile seats first (pij-a...).
